instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Rows where gpa is above the average
output: SELECT * FROM students WHERE gpa > (SELECT AVG(gpa) FROM students);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Row with the highest gpa
output: SELECT * FROM students WHERE gpa = (SELECT MAX(gpa) FROM students);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Row with the lowest gpa
output: SELECT * FROM students WHERE gpa = (SELECT MIN(gpa) FROM students);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Rows where major is in a subquery from students
output: SELECT * FROM students WHERE major IN (SELECT DISTINCT major FROM students);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Rows where major is not in the set of values 1 and 2
output: SELECT * FROM students WHERE major NOT IN (1, 2);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Use EXISTS to find rows where a major appears more than once
output: SELECT * FROM students t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM students t2 WHERE t2.major = t.major GROUP BY t2.major HAVING COUNT(*) > 1);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Subquery in SELECT returning count per major
output: SELECT t.*, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students t2 WHERE t2.major = t.major) AS cnt FROM students t;

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Rows where gpa > the maximum of name plus 100 in subquery
output: SELECT * FROM students WHERE gpa > ((SELECT MAX(gpa) FROM students) + 100);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Second highest gpa using subquery
output: SELECT MAX(gpa) FROM students WHERE gpa < (SELECT MAX(gpa) FROM students);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Correlated subquery: rows whose gpa is above the avg of their major
output: SELECT * FROM students t WHERE gpa > (SELECT AVG(gpa) FROM students t2 WHERE t2.major = t.major);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Columns where gpa is greater than average in their group
output: SELECT * FROM students t WHERE gpa >= (SELECT AVG(gpa) FROM students t2 WHERE t2.major = t.major);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Derived table returning count per major
output: SELECT sub.major, sub.cnt FROM (SELECT major, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM students GROUP BY major) sub WHERE sub.cnt > 2;

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Subquery filtering rows with ANY operator
output: SELECT * FROM students WHERE gpa = ANY (SELECT gpa FROM students WHERE gpa < 50);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Subquery filtering rows with ALL operator
output: SELECT * FROM students WHERE gpa > ALL (SELECT AVG(gpa) FROM students);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Scalar subquery for a single value
output: SELECT (SELECT AVG(gpa) FROM students) AS avg_val;

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Rows matching set from a subquery using IN
output: SELECT * FROM students WHERE major IN (SELECT major FROM students GROUP BY major HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Largest value strictly less than the global maximum
output: SELECT gpa FROM students ORDER BY gpa DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Nested subquery: top values per group based on derived ranking
output: SELECT t.* FROM students t WHERE t.gpa = (SELECT MAX(gpa) FROM students t2 WHERE t2.major = t.major);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Rows where name not present in a sub table
output: SELECT * FROM students WHERE name NOT IN (SELECT name FROM students WHERE gpa > 90);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Subquery used to compare against the overall total
output: SELECT major, SUM(gpa) AS part FROM students GROUP BY major HAVING SUM(gpa) > (SELECT AVG(gpa) FROM students);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Use a subquery to compute rolling reference count
output: SELECT t.major, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students t2 WHERE t2.major <= t.major) AS running FROM students t;

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
EXISTS correlated check to its own table values
output: SELECT * FROM students t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM students t2 WHERE t2.major = t.major AND t2.gpa > t.gpa);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Subquery comparing to the minimum plus a constant
output: SELECT * FROM students WHERE gpa > (SELECT MIN(gpa) FROM students) + 10;

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Subquery returning rows for a top slice group
output: SELECT * FROM students WHERE gpa IN (SELECT gpa FROM students ORDER BY gpa DESC LIMIT 5);

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name, gpa, major)
Subquery joining a derived aggregate
output: SELECT t.* FROM students t JOIN (SELECT major, MAX(gpa) mx FROM students GROUP BY major) a ON a.major = t.major AND a.mx = t.gpa;
